9	/**
10	 * "A camel overcoat unlocks 14 new outfits" is not a query — it is a
11	 * SIMULATION. For each archetypal missing piece, add it to the real closet in
12	 * memory, re-count what becomes buildable, and report the largest increase.
13	 *
14	 * The number is produced by the same eligibility code that builds real outfits,
15	 * so it means exactly what it says rather than approximating it. No AI call.
16	 */
17	
18	/**
19	 * The archetypal pieces we know how to recommend. Deliberately small and
20	 * neutral: the claim is "this unlocks N outfits", and a wilder candidate would
21	 * inflate N while being something the user would never buy.
22	 */
23	export type GapCandidate = { label: string; category: string; colors: string[]; formality: number };
24	
25	export const GAP_CANDIDATES: GapCandidate[] = [
26	  { label: "A camel overcoat", category: "Outerwear", colors: ["camel"], formality: 4 },
27	  { label: "Grey wool trousers", category: "Bottoms", colors: ["grey"], formality: 4 },
28	  { label: "A navy knit", category: "Tops", colors: ["navy"], formality: 3 },
29	  { label: "Brown leather loafers", category: "Shoes", colors: ["brown"], formality: 4 },
30	  { label: "A white oxford shirt", category: "Tops", colors: ["white"], formality: 4 },
31	  { label: "Dark denim", category: "Bottoms", colors: ["denim"], formality: 2 },
32	  { label: "Clean white sneakers", category: "Shoes", colors: ["white"], formality: 2 },
33	];
34	
35	/**
36	 * ⚠️ `buildCandidates` stops at `CAP = 200` (lib/generator/candidates.ts). Any
37	 * closet big enough to exceed that returns 200 both BEFORE and AFTER the
38	 * hypothetical piece, so every `unlocks` is 0 and `biggestGap` returns null —
39	 * for exactly the users who would pay for this screen.
40	 *
41	 * So do not count combos. Count the product of the eligible required slots,
42	 * which is what the cap is truncating, and is the number the claim actually
43	 * means: how many outfits become buildable.
44	 */
45	function countCombos(closet: CandidateItem[], occasions: UiOccasion[], weather: Weather): number {
46	  return occasions.reduce((total, o) => {
47	    const args = {
48	      band: personalBand(o, null),
49	      weather,
50	      // No season preference: the gap is about what the wardrobe can BUILD, and
51	      // season only ever orders and scores (see lib/generator/season.ts). A
52	      // recommendation should not change because it is currently March.
53	      season: undefined,
54	      excludeItemIds: [],
55	      maxAccessories: 0,
56	    };
57	    const by = eligibleByCategory(closet, args);
58	    const slots = REQUIRED_CATEGORIES.map((c) => (by[c] ?? []).length);
59	    // A missing required slot means zero buildable outfits, not a partial count.
60	    return total + (slots.some((n) => n === 0) ? 0 : slots.reduce((a, b) => a * b, 1));
61	  }, 0);
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Which single hypothetical piece would unlock the most outfits.
66	 *
67	 * The number is produced by the SAME code that builds real outfits, so "unlocks
68	 * 14 new outfits" means exactly that — not a heuristic that resembles it.
69	 */
70	export function biggestGap(
71	  closet: CandidateItem[],
72	  occasions: UiOccasion[],
73	  weather: Weather,
74	): { candidate: GapCandidate; unlocks: number } | null {
75	  if (!closet.length) return null;
76	
77	  const before = countCombos(closet, occasions, weather);
78	  let best: { candidate: GapCandidate; unlocks: number } | null = null;
79	
80	  for (const c of GAP_CANDIDATES) {
81	    const hypothetical: CandidateItem = {
82	      id: "__hypothetical__",
83	      category: c.category,
84	      colors: c.colors,
85	      formality: c.formality,
86	      // Untagged on purpose: seasons, material, texture and pattern are all
87	      // "no opinion" values downstream, so the simulated piece is scored as
88	      // neutrally as possible. A hypothetical garment should not win by being
89	      // given flattering tags nobody has bought yet.
90	      seasons: [],
91	      material: null,
92	      pattern: "solid",
93	      texture: null,
94	    };
95	    const unlocks = countCombos([...closet, hypothetical], occasions, weather) - before;
96	    if (unlocks > 0 && (!best || unlocks > best.unlocks)) best = { candidate: c, unlocks };
97	  }
98	  return best;
99	}

I've read all three changed files in full and traced their usage.

**Analysis:**

- `lib/stats/gap.ts` (new): a pure in-memory simulation. Takes the user's own `closet` items, iterates a static const array `GAP_CANDIDATES` (7 hardcoded entries), calls `eligibleByCategory` (a pure filter/sort) for each occasion, and returns which archetypal piece unlocks the most slot-product outfits. No I/O, no shell, no SQL, no FS, no network, no eval, no logging, no deserialization, no template rendering, no auth decisions.
- `lib/generator/candidates.ts` (diff): only change is loosening `season: string` → `season?: string` on `CandidateArgs`. The downstream consumers (`bySeasonFirst`, `inSeason`) already accepted `string | undefined` — no validator or fail-closed gate is being deleted; this is a type-only relaxation with the same runtime behavior it had before.
- `lib/stats/__tests__/gap.test.ts` (new): test file — excluded per the method.

**Sinks touched:** none. **Entry points touched:** none — `biggestGap` is only called by tests (grep confirms no other callers yet). **Registry fanout:** the new `GAP_CANDIDATES` array is not consumed by any security registry (sanitizer/redactor/allowlist) — it's a UI recommendation set. **Resource bounds:** the slot-product `slots.reduce((a,b)=>a*b, 1)` is bounded by the size of a physical wardrobe and runs O(occasions × 8 candidates × items); no attacker-amplifiable path.

No source→sink chain, no authorization boundary crossed, no control regression. Nothing to report.
